title: The Noise-Transmission Burden of Diffusion Network: Why Image Prediction Can Outperform Noise Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2610.34834v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Clean-image prediction ($x$-prediction) and noise prediction yield equivalent population-optimal denoisers, yet can perform very differently in finite diffusion networks. For noisy input $Y_t$ with noise standard deviation $\sigma_t$, a noise predictor $f_{\varepsilon,t}$ induces the clean-image estimate $\widehat X_1=Y_t-\sigma_t f_{\varepsilon,t}(Y_t)$. This reveals a noise-transmission burden: the predictor must preserve information needed to cancel the input corruption. Under Gaussian corruption of $d$-dimensional data, a linear input bottleneck of rank $r<d$ imposes a denoising-error floor $\sigma_t^2(d-r)$ even with unrestricted downstream computation, while the corresponding optimal risk for image prediction remains bounded. EDM attenuates this bottleneck contribution at high noise; exact preconditioning cancels it at every noise level. Without an input bottleneck, assuming exact affine recovery of the noisy patch from the model r

translated_title: 扩散网络的噪声传递负担：为什么图像预测可以优于噪声预测
translated_abstract: 干净图像预测（$x$-prediction）与噪声预测在总体最优去噪器意义上是等价的，但在有限的扩散网络中却可能表现出很大差异。对于噪声标准差为 $\sigma_t$ 的含噪输入 $Y_t$，噪声预测器 $f_{\varepsilon,t}$ 所诱导的干净图像估计为 $\widehat X_1=Y_t-\sigma_t f_{\varepsilon,t}(Y_t)$。这揭示了一种“噪声传递负担”：预测器必须保留用于抵消输入污染的信息。在对 $d$ 维数据施加高斯污染的情况下，一个秩为 $r<d$ 的线性输入瓶颈即使在不限制下游计算的情况下，也会强加一个 $\sigma_t^2(d-r)$ 的去噪误差下界，而图像预测对应的最优风险则保持有界。EDM 在高噪声水平下会削弱这一瓶颈的影响；而精确的预处理（preconditioning）则能在每个噪声水平上完全消除它。在没有输入瓶颈的情况下，假设含噪图像块可以从模型中被精确仿射恢复……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文揭示了扩散模型噪声预测参数化带来的“噪声传递负担”——网络必须保留输入噪声信息以抵消污染，在低秩输入瓶颈下导致随噪声增长的去噪误差下界，而图像预测不受此限制，从而解释了为什么在有限网络中图像预测可以优于噪声预测。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies a "noise-transmission burden" in noise-prediction diffusion networks—the model must preserve input noise information to cancel corruption—which imposes a noise-growing denoising error floor under low-rank input bottlenecks, explaining why image prediction can outperform noise prediction in finite networks.
